differ: Presence: bodily for Rome and the Lutherans, real but spiritual for the Reformed, and for the memorial view a remembrance of his death.
The elements: only Rome teaches that the bread ceases to be bread. All three Protestant confessions say it remains bread.
The unbeliever: Lutherans confess he receives Christ's body and blood to judgment; Westminster says he receives only the outward elements.
Frequency: Rome and Augsburg set a pattern; Westminster and the Baptist Faith and Message set none.

sources.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church, The Sacrament of the Eucharist
sources.quote: This change the holy Catholic Church has fittingly and properly called transubstantiation.
sources.notes: Paragraph 1376 (quoting Trent): 'a change of the whole substance of the bread into the substance of the body of Christ'. 1374: 'the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ and, therefore, the whole Christ is truly, really, and substantially contained.'

sources.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church, Holy Communion
sources.quote: Anyone conscious of a grave sin must receive the sacrament of Reconciliation before coming to communion.
sources.notes: Paragraph 1385. Paragraph 1389: the faithful must receive 'at least once a year', and the Church 'strongly encourages the faithful to receive the holy Eucharist on Sundays and feast days, or more often still, even daily.'

sources.title: Augsburg Confession, Article X: Of the Lord's Supper
sources.quote: the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present, and are distributed to those who eat the Supper of the Lord
sources.notes: Triglot translation. The old /augsburg-confession/article-x/ URL redirects here.

sources.title: Augsburg Confession, Article XXIV: Of the Mass
sources.quote: we hold one communion every holy-day, and, if any desire the Sacrament, also on other days
sources.notes: Also: 'For none are admitted except they be first examined.'

sources.title: Formula of Concord, Epitome, Article VII: Of the Holy Supper
sources.quote: not only the true believers [in Christ] and the worthy, but also the unworthy and unbelievers, receive the true body and blood of Christ
sources.notes: Also: the body and blood 'are truly distributed and received with the bread and wine'; 'because of the sacramental union'; rejects 'The papistic transubstantiation'.

sources.title: Westminster Confession of Faith, Chapter 29: Of the Lord's Supper
sources.quote: as really, but spiritually, present to the faith of believers in that ordinance, as the elements themselves are to their outward senses
sources.notes: 29.5: 'in substance and nature, they still remain truly and only bread and wine'. 29.3: the elements are set apart 'from a common to an holy use'. 29.8: the ignorant and wicked 'receive the outward elements ... yet, they receive not the thing signified thereby' and are 'unworthy of the Lord's table'. The Confession sets no frequency.

sources.title: The Baptist Faith and Message 2000, Article VII
sources.quote: The Lord's Supper is a symbolic act of obedience whereby members of the church, through partaking of the bread and the fruit of the vine, memorialize the death of the Redeemer and anticipate His second coming.
sources.notes: Same article, on baptism: 'it is prerequisite to the privileges of church membership and to the Lord's Supper.' The page uses a curly apostrophe in Lord's. No frequency is set.
